newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM sees no government grain imports in '97.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM sees no government grain imports in '97.

text.p: The Russian government, absent from world grain markets for at past three years, will not import grain this year, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday.
"We haven't bought grain for three years, and this year we won't be buying either," Interfax news agency quoted him as telling farmers in Suzdal, in central Russia.
"In general, from now on we're not going to buy grain -- we're going to sell it."
Chernomyrdin did not give a prediction for Russia's net grain crop, which the government has forecast flat at at least 70 million tonnes.
But he did say farmers would need to learn to pay for inputs instead of relying on state-issued supplies and credits, a woefully inefficient mainstay of the largely unreformed system.
"We're not going to just hand things out on credit -- things must be bought," he said.
Russia has had two poor grain harvests in a row, with last year's output of 69.3 million tonnes one of the worst in decades.
Some officials and independent analysts have said the cycle may be broken this year and that output could be as high as 80 million tonnes.
